/videos/measures-of-central-tendency-101.summary: Discover how mean, median, and mode can impact your UX insights. Learn 3 key tips to consider when deciding which one to use for your data.

/videos/destination-pages-vs-transition-.title: Destination Pages vs. Transition Pages
/videos/destination-pages-vs-transition-.summary: Destination pages fulfill users' information needs through detailed content, while transition pages guide them toward these destinations through navigation and brief overviews. Content prioritization based on user goals and information needs is key in designing both pages.

/videos/promptframes-using-ai-content/.title: Promptframes: Using AI-Content to Inspire Feedback
/videos/promptframes-using-ai-content/.summary: Promptframes combine traditional wireframes with AI prompts to create content-rich prototypes. Ditch confusing placeholders using AI to quickly inspire feedback from your collaborators and users.

/videos/in-person-usability-testing/.title: A Case for Returning to In-Person Usability Testing
/videos/in-person-usability-testing/.summary: In-person usability testing provides insights remote testing can miss. It offers unique benefits, such as building rapport, observing non-verbal cues, and providing immersive experiences for stakeholders that enhance understanding.

/videos/design-influence-by-business-lan.title: Strengthen Your Design Influence by Speaking the Language of Business
/videos/design-influence-by-business-lan.summary: Design doesn’t have much respect in most companies. To change this you must learn to speak the language of business.

/videos/seq-vs-sus/.title: SEQ vs. SUS
/videos/seq-vs-sus/.summary: Pair qualitative methods with quantitative metrics like the System Usability Scale (SUS) for benchmarking and the Single Ease Question (SEQ) for task-level insights. Use both carefully with qualitative data.

/videos/ux-research-job-interviews/.title: UX Research Job Interviews: 5 Things to Showcase
/videos/ux-research-job-interviews/.summary: Set yourself apart in UX research job interviews and leave a memorable impact on interviewers.

/videos/error-message-scoring-rubric/.title: Check Error-Message Quality with a Scoring Rubric
/videos/error-message-scoring-rubric/.summary: Use a scoring rubric to objectively assess error message quality based on their visibility, communication, and efficiency. Involve your colleagues and reduce skepticism of your analysis.

/videos/object-oriented-ux-ooux/.title: Object-Oriented UX (OOUX)
/videos/object-oriented-ux-ooux/.summary: Identifying objects, their characteristics, and relationships in an experience can help simplify designs and make systems easier to use by aligning with people's mental models. (Credit: Sophia Prater)

/videos/wizard-of-oz-method/.title: Wizard of Oz Method in UX
/videos/wizard-of-oz-method/.summary: There are five steps to run the Wizard of Oz Method, a moderated research method in which a user interacts with an interface that appears to be automated but is actually controlled to some degree by a person.

/videos/content-dispersion-in-mobile-fir.title: Content Dispersion: The Downside of Mobile-first Design
/videos/content-dispersion-in-mobile-fir.summary: Content dispersion occurs when the content of a responsive webpage appears overly large and stretched out on large laptop or desktop screens. What negative affects can it create?

/videos/sample-sizes-for-qualitative-stu.title: Sample Sizes for Qualitative Studies
/videos/sample-sizes-for-qualitative-stu.summary: When choosing your sample size for a qualitative research study, consider these three factors: the diversity of your target group, your research scope, and the researcher’s skill level.

/videos/ai-for-tone/.title: AI for Tone: Avoid Sounding Like a Robot
/videos/ai-for-tone/.summary: Learn how to use AI chats like ChatGPT to write copy that doesn’t sound like a robot wrote it.

/videos/custom-events-in-analytics/.title: Unlock Powerful UX Insights with Custom Events in Analytics
/videos/custom-events-in-analytics/.summary: Discover how custom events in analytics can transform your UX strategy by providing detailed insights into critical user behaviors, allowing for better-informed design decisions.

/videos/the-danger-of-defaults/.title: The Danger of Defaults
/videos/the-danger-of-defaults/.summary: Assume that users will not change defaults and plan for this in your designs. Ask yourself 3 questions to create good defaults.

/videos/attitudinal-vs-behavioral-resear.title: Attitudinal vs. Behavioral Research
/videos/attitudinal-vs-behavioral-resear.summary: Explore the difference between attitudinal and behavioral UX research. Learn how combining these methods offers a complete view of user interactions and perceptions.

/videos/design-systems-vs-style-guides/.title: Design Systems vs. Style Guides
/videos/design-systems-vs-style-guides/.summary: A design system is a complete set of standards intended to manage design at scale, while a style guide is a piece of documentation that provides specific style guidance.

/videos/ux-metrics-are-like-beans/.title: UX Metrics Are Like Beans
/videos/ux-metrics-are-like-beans/.summary: Common UX metrics can be grouped into three types: continuous, discrete, and binary. Continuous metrics occur on a smooth spectrum, like time. Discrete metrics have regular intervals between them, such as satisfaction score. Binary metrics have two possible values, like pass or fail.

/videos/upfront-vs-continuous-discovery/.title: Upfront vs. Continuous Discovery
/videos/upfront-vs-continuous-discovery/.summary: Upfront and continuous discovery are two approaches to implementing discovery in product development. Both approaches help teams solve real problems.

/videos/cookie-permissions-user-types/.title: Cookie Permissions: 5 Common User Types
/videos/cookie-permissions-user-types/.summary: Users’ willingness to share data and their interactions with cookie permission box options vary quite drastically, falling into these five common user types: The Denier, The Skeptic, The Tech-Savvy, The Impatient, and The Enthusiast.

/videos/ux-goals-vs-okrs-kpis/.title: UX Goals vs. OKRs vs. KPIs
/videos/ux-goals-vs-okrs-kpis/.summary: Learn what UX Goals, OKRs, and KPIs are and how to use them as a framework to measure the success and progress of UX work.

/videos/surveys-in-the-design-process/.title: Types of Surveys to Run Throughout the Design Process
/videos/surveys-in-the-design-process/.summary: There are lots of types of UX surveys. Which one to use depends on your research goal and where you are in the design process.

/videos/ux-in-sprint-reviews/.title: Should UX Be in Sprint Reviews?
/videos/ux-in-sprint-reviews/.summary: UX should be included in an Agile scrum team’s Sprint Review to share knowledge that can improve product strategy, answer tricky stakeholder questions, and increase visibility for UX work.

/videos/conduct-competitive-usability-ev.title: How to Conduct a Competitive Usability Evaluation
/videos/conduct-competitive-usability-ev.summary: Competitive usability evaluations help you understand how your competitors solve certain design problems and how you might outperform them. These evaluations are often performed at the beginning of design projects to shift their direction toward areas of opportunity.

/videos/ux-roadmap-tool-tradeoffs/.title: UX Roadmap Tool Tradeoffs
/videos/ux-roadmap-tool-tradeoffs/.summary: Find the right UX roadmap tool: PowerPoint, spreadsheets, whiteboards, or project management tools. Consider your project complexity, team size, and requirements.

/videos/cyclical-design-trends/.title: Why 90’s Designs Are Coming Back
/videos/cyclical-design-trends/.summary: Understanding the cyclical nature of design trends allows us to build on the past and fulfill the evolving needs of users. 3 examples of returning trends are neumorphism, dark mode, and gradients.

/videos/latch-framework/.title: Organize Information with "LATCH"
/videos/latch-framework/.summary: The LATCH framework organizes information based on location, alphabet, time, category, and hierarchy. This method helps transform complex datasets into meaningful structures, facilitating effective navigation.

/videos/efficient-error-messages/.title: Create Efficient Error Messages
/videos/efficient-error-messages/.summary: You need efficient error messages to keep users engaged in their workflow. Follow these four efficiency guidelines to design error messages that respect users' effort and offer time-saving guidance.

/videos/avoid-deceptive-patterns/.title: Don’t Trick Users: 2 Ways to Avoid Deceptive Design Patterns
/videos/avoid-deceptive-patterns/.summary: Deceptive patterns harm your organization’s long-term goals. Ask yourself these 2 questions to proactively avoid deceiving or tricking users.

/videos/generalist-vs-specialist/.title: Generalist vs. Specialist UX Designers
/videos/generalist-vs-specialist/.summary: Should you be a specialized or generalist UX designer? Both roles offer substantial value to a team and unique perspectives for solving UX challenges.

/videos/why-40-participants-quantitative.title: Why Use 40 Participants in Quantitative UX Research?
/videos/why-40-participants-quantitative.summary: 40 is the optimal sample size for many quantitative UX studies, ensuring a balance of precision, risk, and practicality.

/videos/coding-thematic-analysis/.title: Coding in Thematic Analysis
/videos/coding-thematic-analysis/.summary: By coding qualitative data, we can see trends and patterns, which helps us find themes. For an efficient process, create some starter codes, start broad, and use short, clear labels.

/videos/ux-team-charters/.title: UX Team Charters
/videos/ux-team-charters/.summary: A UX team charter clarifies a team's purpose, roles, and goals to improve efficiency and collaboration. It's a commitment to shared values and working methods to make the UX team's vision actionable.

/videos/roadmaps-vs-project-timelines/.title: Roadmaps vs. Project Timelines
/videos/roadmaps-vs-project-timelines/.summary: Learn how roadmaps can guide product team strategy and project timelines guide execution.

/videos/error-message-communication-guid.title: Error Messages: 4 Guidelines for Effective Communication
/videos/error-message-communication-guid.summary: Communicate effectively with your error messages by using human-readable language, concisely and precisely describing the issue, offering constructive advice, and not blaming the user.

/videos/ux-resumes-seasoned-professional.title: UX Resumes: 10 Tips for Seasoned Professionals
/videos/ux-resumes-seasoned-professional.summary: You have a lot of UX experience, but how best to communicate it to a hiring manager on your resume? Use these 10 tips to make your hard-won achievements persuasive, even at a glance.

/videos/break-into-design/.title: How to Break Into Design: Don’s Advice
/videos/break-into-design/.summary: Use your unique background to break into the field of UX Design.

/videos/practical-vs-statistical-signifi.title: Practical vs. Statistical Significance
/videos/practical-vs-statistical-signifi.summary: Statistical significance does not always equal practical significance. A difference may be statistically significant without having any meaningful impact in real life. Conversely, practical differences may not always achieve statistical significance.

/videos/stakeholder-personas-vs-profiles.title: Stakeholder Personas vs. Stakeholder Profiles
/videos/stakeholder-personas-vs-profiles.summary: Leverage stakeholder personas and profiles to engage stakeholders effectively and ensure success in UX projects.

/videos/design-thinking-6-rules/.title: The 6 Rules of Design Thinking
/videos/design-thinking-6-rules/.summary: Follow the 6 rules of design thinking during workshops to help participants embrace the core principles of design thinking and ensure successful outcomes.

/videos/skeleton-screens-vs-progress-bar.title: Skeleton Screens vs. Progress Bars vs. Spinners
/videos/skeleton-screens-vs-progress-bar.summary: Skeleton screens, progress bars, and spinners all indicate the system is loading content, but they serve different purposes and work best in different contexts.

/videos/livestream-ecommerce-tips/.title: Livestream Ecommerce: 7 Tips for Good UX
/videos/livestream-ecommerce-tips/.summary: Livestream shopping allows real-time interaction and purchasing. To excel, businesses should choose the right platform, act professionally, offer rewards, streamline purchasing, and promote sessions strategically.

/videos/intranet-success-metrics/.title: How to Measure Intranet Performance: 3 Key Success Metrics
/videos/intranet-success-metrics/.summary: Measure your intranet's effectiveness with strategic metrics for usage patterns, employee engagement, and satisfaction ratings. Improve your organization through insightful intranet analysis.

/videos/research-repositories-101/.title: Research Repositories 101
/videos/research-repositories-101/.summary: A research repository is a central place where user research is stored. The tool used, how contributions are made, and how research is stored can impact its adoption.

/videos/mvp-isnt-release1/.title: MVP: Why It Isn't Always Release 1
/videos/mvp-isnt-release1/.summary: A minimum viable product (MVP) is a reasonable representation of your product that maximizes feedback on your core value proposition. It doesn’t need to be release one, but can be a simple experiment.

/videos/swot-analysis/.title: What Is a SWOT Analysis?
/videos/swot-analysis/.summary: A SWOT Analysis is a framework to analyze the position of a company or product experience relative to others in the market. Its four quadrants offer prompts to help teams identify specific factors that may impact their success.

/videos/user-testing-older-adults/.title: User Testing with Older Adults
/videos/user-testing-older-adults/.summary: When conducting usability testing with older adults, understand the unique needs of participants in this age group and adjust your test setup and tasks accordingly.

/videos/personas-are-living-documents/.title: Personas Are Living Documents: Design Them to Evolve
/videos/personas-are-living-documents/.summary: Design personas to evolve and change over time to secure their longevity. Design personas in a way that allows for updates when significant insights emerge, ensuring they remain relevant and maintain their usefulness over time.

/videos/castle-framework/.title: CASTLE: Measure UX in Workplace Software
/videos/castle-framework/.summary: Discover the CASTLE framework for measuring UX in workplace software, an alternative to Google's HEART model.

/videos/quantify-design-impact/.title: Quantify the Business Impact of Your Design
/videos/quantify-design-impact/.summary: Learn how to sell design recommendations to business stakeholders by quantifying the impact of design changes in business terms.

/videos/success-rate-vs-completion-rate/.title: Success Rate vs. Completion Rate
/videos/success-rate-vs-completion-rate/.summary: Measure completion rate when users follow a linear process with a fixed number of steps; use success rate when there are multiple ways to accomplish a task.

/videos/smartwatch-notification-formula/.title: The Smartwatch Notification Formula
/videos/smartwatch-notification-formula/.summary: Maximize the value of your smartwatch notifications by making them personally relevant, appropriately timed, non-repetitive, and sufficiently informative.

/videos/what-is-user-research/.title: What Is User Research?
/videos/what-is-user-research/.summary: The goal of user research is to identify ways to improve a product's design based on evidence rather than opinions.

/videos/flat-vs-deep-hierarchies/.title: Flat vs. Deep Hierarchies in Information Architecture (IA)
/videos/flat-vs-deep-hierarchies/.summary: Information can be structured in flat or deep hierarchies, each with their own set of benefits and drawbacks.

/videos/why-ux-roadmaps-fail/.title: 4 Reasons Your UX Roadmaps Are Not Working and What to Do Instead
/videos/why-ux-roadmaps-fail/.summary: Enhance UX roadmaps by focusing on themes instead of features, flexible timelines, team prioritization, and regular revisions.

/videos/homepage-design-mistakes/.title: Homepage Design: 4 Common Mistakes
/videos/homepage-design-mistakes/.summary: Enhance your homepage design by avoiding false floors, providing clear scrolling cues, adhering to familiar web standards, and creating a distinct visual hierarchy to focus user attention.

/videos/structured-content/.title: Structured Content: Benefits and Tips
/videos/structured-content/.summary: Structured content allows for flexible information presentation across channels. It supports consistency, efficient content operations, and adaptability with UI design changes.

/videos/competitive-reviews-vs-competiti.title: Competitive Reviews vs. Competitive Research
/videos/competitive-reviews-vs-competiti.summary: There is more than one way to conduct a competitive evaluation. This video describes the difference between a competitive review and competitive research.

/videos/international-usability-testing/.title: International Usability Testing: 3 Factors to Consider
/videos/international-usability-testing/.summary: International usability testing examines how people from different regions use products. For successful testing, decide on the format, ensure clear communication despite language barriers, and select a facilitator familiar with the local context.

/videos/video-evidence/.title: Seeing Is Believing: Using Video Evidence When Presenting Research to Stakeholders
/videos/video-evidence/.summary: Video evidence is a strong UX storytelling tool that helps you improve comprehension, build empathy, and overcome skepticism when communicating research findings to stakeholders.

/videos/breakpoints/.title: Breakpoints in Responsive Design: What & Why
/videos/breakpoints/.summary: Breakpoints determine when a webpage may adjust to different layouts. They help designers (and developers) maintain layout consistency across multiple screen sizes, orientations, and devices.

/videos/15-user-research-methods-beyond-.title: 15 User Research Methods to Know Beyond Usability Testing
/videos/15-user-research-methods-beyond-.summary: Explore 15 user research methods beyond usability testing. We describe 5 scenarios where these methods offer a broad spectrum of insights for a better understanding of users.

/videos/error-message-visibility/.title: How to Increase the Visibility of Error Messages
/videos/error-message-visibility/.summary: Error messages can be a crucial point in the user experience. To be effective, they must be clearly visible, which can be accomplished by displaying them close to the error's source, using noticeable, redundant, and accessible indicators, designing them based on their impact, and avoiding displaying them prematurely.

/videos/cognitive-load/.title: What Is Cognitive Load?
/videos/cognitive-load/.summary: Follow these 3 tips to reduce cognitive load and help your users: avoid visual clutter, build on existing mental models, and offload tasks.

/videos/storytelling-in-ux-job-interview.title: 10 Steps for Better Storytelling in UX Job Interviews
/videos/storytelling-in-ux-job-interview.summary: Searching for a UX job and want an edge on your competition? Stop endlessly iterating over your portfolio and start practicing storytelling to ace your UX job interviews.

/videos/not-too-late-to-use-ai/.title: You're Not Too Late to Use AI
/videos/not-too-late-to-use-ai/.summary: Manage your AI anxiety with two quick tips: small experiments and a news diet. Experiment with day-to-day communication and drafting with AI, as integrating AI into your research process. To avoid news overwhelm, subscribe to three weekly sources of information: a newsletter, an optimistic writing source, and a skeptical writing source.

/videos/research-participant-database/.title: Create Your Own Research-Participant Database
/videos/research-participant-database/.summary: Make user research and recruiting more efficient by keeping your own database of research participants. What’s important when choosing tools? What data should you store, and how should you govern the use of the database?

/videos/csd-matrix/.title: Using a CSD Matrix in Discovery
/videos/csd-matrix/.summary: CSD matrices organize project information by Certainties, Suppositions, and Doubts. Use the framework to make decisions, form hypotheses, and address unknowns in discovery. (Credit: Tennyson Pinheiro, Luis Alt and the team at Livework São Paulo.)

/videos/delightful-ux/.title: Delightful UX Is Like a 3-Legged Stool
/videos/delightful-ux/.summary: Delight can be experienced viscerally, behaviorally, and reflectively. A delightful design must consider all three of these pillars.

/videos/interactive-ux-maps/.title: Interactive UX Maps 101
/videos/interactive-ux-maps/.summary: Interactive UX Maps are high-fidelity maps used as a way to engage stakeholders with real user data in relationship to specific findings.

/videos/tabs-vs-accordions/.title: Tabs vs. Accordions: When to Use Each
/videos/tabs-vs-accordions/.summary: Tabs and accordions organize and layer content on the same page. Tabs suit a few long sections, while accordions fit many short ones. Choose based on your content structure and user needs for optimal layout.

/videos/conduct-heuristic-evaluation/.title: How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation
/videos/conduct-heuristic-evaluation/.summary: Learn how to systematically review your product to find potential usability and experience problems.

/videos/ai-not-ready-for-ux/.title: AI Isn't Ready for UX Design
/videos/ai-not-ready-for-ux/.summary: Our research and evaluation show that there are currently few design-specific AI tools that meaningfully enhance UX design workflows. As of Spring 2024, AI isn’t ready for designers to take advantage of them.

/videos/what-is-ux-not/.title: What Is UX (Not)?
/videos/what-is-ux-not/.summary: While UX is often conflated with limited concepts such as usability, interactions, and technology, a holistic user experience considers a person's thoughts, emotions, and actions.

/videos/livestream-for-business/.title: Is Livestream Selling Right for Your Business?
/videos/livestream-for-business/.summary: Livestream ecommerce offers a dynamic platform for real-time interaction and product demonstration. Follow these tips to determine if livestream selling is worth it for your business.

/videos/cookie-permissions-guidelines/.title: Cookie Permissions: 6 Design Guidelines
/videos/cookie-permissions-guidelines/.summary: Design cookie permissions that strike the balance between respecting user privacy and being user-friendly.

/videos/7-steps-collaboration/.title: Successful Projects: 7 Steps for Better Collaboration
/videos/7-steps-collaboration/.summary: Effective collaboration can be challenging, yet it is crucial for successful outcomes. By following 7 steps for better collaboration, you can avoid the most common issues and set yourself up for success.

/videos/journey-management-competencies/.title: The 3 Competencies of Journey Management
/videos/journey-management-competencies/.summary: Managing journeys requires a continuous practice of 3 interdependent competencies: collecting insights, analyzing them to drive design strategy, and orchestrating journey experiences for users.

/videos/present-research-responsively/.title: How to Present UX Research Results Responsibly
/videos/present-research-responsively/.summary: Presenting study data to stakeholders is a crucial step of most projects. Make sure to present your data truthfully and responsibly to avoid costly negative outcomes and reputation loss. Indicate who your data represents and communicate the limitations of your findings.

/videos/intranet-feedback/.title: Intranet Feedback Features
/videos/intranet-feedback/.summary: The input gathered from intranet feedback tools helps to enhance the content, personalize the experience, and signal the need for more in-depth research to keep the intranet employee-centered.

/videos/ux-job-meteor/.title: Have Your UX Job Wish Come True with METEOR
/videos/ux-job-meteor/.summary: UX job interview questions and whiteboarding challenges that ask you to resolve a situation are tough. Remember METEOR to structure your problem-solving process and give effective answers.

/videos/credit-for-usability/.title: Why the UX Team Doesn't Get the Credit
/videos/credit-for-usability/.summary: The easier designs are to use, the less users tend to think about the work that went into making them that way. We know good designs are largely the result of your careful efforts — thank you.

/videos/whitespace/.title: What is Whitespace?
/videos/whitespace/.summary: Whitespace is an effective principle to achieve a balanced design, making it easier for your users to scan and read. Consider using a consistent spacing system and the proximity principle to achieve a balanced use of whitespace.

/videos/in-page-links/.title: In-Page Links: 3 Usability Tips
/videos/in-page-links/.summary: In-page links help users navigate to specific content sections on the same page. For effective use, use descriptive headings that match the destination, and clearly distinguish in-page links from other links.

/videos/remote-workshop-tips/.title: 3 Tips for More Engaging Remote UX Workshops
/videos/remote-workshop-tips/.summary: Break the virtual barrier in remote UX workshops by incorporating tangible objects, using different virtual spaces, and varying participant contribution methods.

/videos/zeigarnik-effect/.title: How to Use the Zeigarnik Effect in UX
/videos/zeigarnik-effect/.summary: The Zeigarnik effect suggests that unfinished tasks are more memorable than completed ones. In UX design, we can leverage this effect to encourage user engagement and task completion.

/videos/error-messages-101/.title: Error Messages 101
/videos/error-messages-101/.summary: When humans interact with computers, mistakes and misunderstandings are inevitable. In these situations, good error messages are a vital tool to avoid frustrations and provide a satisfying user experience.

/videos/card-sorting-why-when/.title: Card Sorting: Why & When
/videos/card-sorting-why-when/.summary: Card sorting studies help understand how users naturally categorize information. This information can help with creating a product's information architecture (IA) that matches users' mental models.

/videos/personas-101/.title: Personas 101
/videos/personas-101/.summary: Personas are personified representations of real information about our target audience that enable us to design with real customers in mind. They help us align ideas and apply what we know.

/videos/measurement-error/.title: Measurement Error in UX Research
/videos/measurement-error/.summary: Measurement error is the error we introduce when we measure or observe something about our users. It can come from different sources, such as the number of participants, individual variation between participants, testing environment, or other outside factors. This video helps understand and communicate such measurement errors.

/videos/tips-for-effective-feedback/.title: UX Design Critiques: 3 Tips for Effective Feedback
/videos/tips-for-effective-feedback/.summary: Giving feedback as young designers can feel overwhelming and may often stem from a lack of confidence. Here are 3 tips to help you build confidence providing feedback in UX design critiques. Remember that your insights are valuable, structure your feedback, and provide balanced feedback.

/videos/role-of-design/.title: The Role of Design
/videos/role-of-design/.summary: Don Norman explains the role of design and how designers can gain more respect.

/videos/junior-designer-mistakes/.title: 5 Common Mistakes Junior Designers Make
/videos/junior-designer-mistakes/.summary: There are 5 common mistakes junior designers make. They focus on the look instead of usability, commit type crimes, work outside of design systems, lack confidence when presenting their designs, and ask for feedback too often.

/videos/ux-job-interviews-star/.title: Shine in Your UX Job Interviews with STAR
/videos/ux-job-interviews-star/.summary: Confusing and vague answers during your UX job interview can dim your chances. Remember STAR to communicate with poise and confidence.

/videos/frequency-in-qualitative-data/.title: Frequency ≠ Importance in Qualitative Data
/videos/frequency-in-qualitative-data/.summary: Counting how frequently something is mentioned in qualitative data will not always show you what's most important. Sometimes, the most valuable insights are mentioned only once.

/videos/ux-roles-responsibilities/.title: RACI for UX Roles and Responsibilities
/videos/ux-roles-responsibilities/.summary: Clarify roles and tasks with a RACI matrix to identify collaboration points and ensure smoother workflows in product development.

/videos/responsive-web-design/.title: Responsive Web Design: 3 Key Fundamentals
/videos/responsive-web-design/.summary: Responsive web design adapts to various screen sizes while emphasizing developmental efficiency over device-specific designs. It's key to prioritize content based on different contexts of use across devices and create a cohesive experience for all users.

/videos/flow-state/.title: Encouraging Flow State in Products
/videos/flow-state/.summary: A Flow State is an enjoyable mental state of extreme focus provided by the perfect balance of challenge and skill. Follow our 3 tips to design products that allow users to enter the flow state.

/videos/measuring-designops-reach/.title: Measuring DesignOps with REACH
/videos/measuring-designops-reach/.summary: DesignOps success is difficult to measure. Use the REACH framework (Results, Efficiency, Ability, Clarity, Health) to identify and triangulate relevant DesignOps metrics.

/videos/transactional-notification/.title: Transactional Notification 101
/videos/transactional-notification/.summary: Transactional notifications are concise, timely messages related to customer-company interactions. For effective notifications, it's crucial to have a clear subject line, provide all necessary transaction details, and ensure easy options for users to unsubscribe.

/videos/ux-maturity-communication-activi.title: Improving UX Maturity: 10 Communication Activities
/videos/ux-maturity-communication-activi.summary: Design teams can face challenges caused by their organization's low UX maturity. This is a short guide of 10 communication activities to increase your organization's UX maturity and eliminate or decrease these common challenges.

/videos/power-law-of-learning/.title: Power Law of Learning: How to Launch New Designs Successfully
/videos/power-law-of-learning/.summary: Time on task decreases with the number of times the task has been performed in the past. As a result, a new version of an app translates into a temporary productivity loss for its users.

/videos/product-led-growth/.title: Product-Led Growth & UX
/videos/product-led-growth/.summary: The product-led growth model enables users to try a product or service before paying. This video offers three tips for UX professionals to support a product-led user experience: Connect changes to metrics, interview/survey users, and compare behavior and feedback.

/videos/resumes-ux-students-and-graduate.title: UX Resumes for Students and Graduates: Guidelines and Tips
/videos/resumes-ux-students-and-graduate.summary: Sometimes UX students and graduates struggle to create their resumes. Learn which content to prioritize and how to convey it to persuade UX hiring managers and successfully start your UX career.

/videos/prototyping-tool/.title: UX Prototyping: 5 Factors for Selecting the Right Tool
/videos/prototyping-tool/.summary: Choosing the right prototyping tool can be difficult among the many options available. There are 5 key factors to consider when selecting the best fit for your project or team: project type and goals, cost, tool capabilities, learnability and ease of use, and stakeholder buy-in.

/videos/steeple-framework/.title: STEEPLE: Building Contextual Knowledge
/videos/steeple-framework/.summary: STEEPLE is an acronym to help teams identify specific categories of external, contextual factors that may impact the success of your product or service. Being conscious of these factors can ensure your team reduces risks in future design strategies or investments.

/videos/avoid-accordions/.title: Accordions: 5 Scenarios to Avoid Them
/videos/avoid-accordions/.summary: Avoid using accordions when: 1. Users need access to most content; 2. There's little visible content on the page; 3. Content is complex with multiple levels; 4. Content can't be effectively chunked; 5. An uninterrupted reading flow is prioritized.

/videos/quantitative-research-errors/.title: Common Errors in Quantitative Research
/videos/quantitative-research-errors/.summary: False positives and negatives are common errors in quantitative studies that can lead to harmful business decisions. To avoid these mistakes recruit large enough sample sizes, representative participants, and control for confounding variables.

/videos/ai-intranets-features/.title: AI on Intranets: 5 Valuable Features
/videos/ai-intranets-features/.summary: NN/g’s 2023 Intranet Design Annual winners used AI for chatbots, tool recommendations, career guides, virtual assistants, and personalized communications to boost productivity.

/videos/accessibility-widget/.title: Accessibility Widgets Are Not Enough for Screen-Reader Users
/videos/accessibility-widget/.summary: Website accessibility widgets add little value in making your site accessible to users with partial or no vision.

/videos/portfolio-updates/.title: UX Portfolio Updates: A New Year's Resolution
/videos/portfolio-updates/.summary: Is your UX portfolio woefully outdated? Use this simple technique every new year to capture your important achievements and make the task more manageable.

/videos/data-findings-insights/.title: Data vs. Findings vs. Insights
/videos/data-findings-insights/.summary: Data refers to unanalyzed user observations, findings capture patterns among data points, and insights are the actionable opportunities based on research and business goals.

/videos/better-dot-voting/.title: Make Dot Voting Better
/videos/better-dot-voting/.summary: Think beyond the dot in your next UX workshop! Variations of dot voting such as heat mapping and dot coding add context and facilitate deeper discussion during UX prioritization activities.

/videos/mobile-table-of-contents/.title: Tables of Contents on Mobile
/videos/mobile-table-of-contents/.summary: Tables of contents show mobile users an overview of the information on the page and allow them to easily access the piece of content that is relevant to them. Two possible implementations involve in-page links and accordions.

/videos/goldilocks-principle/.title: The Goldilocks Principle for Prototyping
/videos/goldilocks-principle/.summary: The Goldilocks Principle says to aim for prototypes that are just right for your user research needs and will get an honest reaction from participants.

/videos/cultural-difference/.title: Cultural Differences in User Research Facilitation
/videos/cultural-difference/.summary: Cultural differences can negatively impact study outcomes when conducting international user research studies. Identify these differences and use 3 techniques to lower their effects.

/videos/squint-test/.title: Squint Test
/videos/squint-test/.summary: Use the squint test to identify elements that catch attention and assess the visual hierarchy in your design. Ensure high-priority content stands out visually.

/videos/journey-management-vs-service-de.title: Journey Management vs. Service Design
/videos/journey-management-vs-service-de.summary: Service design is an active effort to design a service solution for a customer need, while journey management is an ongoing effort to improve or sustain the quality of an existing service or journey.

/videos/user-feedback/.title: User Feedback: 5 Guidelines
/videos/user-feedback/.summary: Follow these five guidelines to enhance both the quantity and quality of feedback received from your users.

/videos/risk-statements/.title: UX Risk Statements to Influence Stakeholders
/videos/risk-statements/.summary: UX professionals can use UX risk statements to structure their communication, negotiate with the business, and advocate for or against particular activities or approaches.

/videos/research-repositories/.title: Research Repositories for UX Benchmarking Studies
/videos/research-repositories/.summary: A benchmark research repository helps conduct valid benchmarking studies. It should include all the details and the raw data of your UX-benchmarking study.

/videos/sprint-reviews/.title: Sprint Reviews: Prioritize Your Users
/videos/sprint-reviews/.summary: Prioritize users in sprint reviews by demoing features from the user's perspective and creating outcome-based sprint goals.

/videos/eliza-effect/.title: ELIZA Effect: Why We Fall in Love with AI
/videos/eliza-effect/.summary: The ELIZA effect describes users' tendency to quickly attribute human characteristics to artificial systems when the interaction feels human-like. This is why people fall in love with AI.

/videos/dot-voting-problems/.title: Dot Voting: 3 Common Problems
/videos/dot-voting-problems/.summary: Dot-voting activities are prone to 3 common pitfalls: choice overload, choice imbalance, and social bias. Smart planning can help you avoid them.

/videos/pilot-test/.title: Always Pilot Test User Research Studies
/videos/pilot-test/.summary: Running a pilot test for a user research study enables you to assess the study's effectiveness and avoid common problems in the main study.

/videos/mobile-images/.title: Images on Mobile
/videos/mobile-images/.summary: Decorative images should not be used on mobile, as they lengthen the page and make it load more slowly. Use images only if they add informational value to your page.

/videos/organizing-ux-feedback/.title: Organizing UX Feedback
/videos/organizing-ux-feedback/.summary: Use an Action, Persuade, Clarify framework to efficiently organize feedback on UX work.

/videos/personas-vs-analytics-segments/.title: Personas vs. Analytics Segments
/videos/personas-vs-analytics-segments/.summary: Avoid creating personas from analytics data alone. Personas are artifacts that aim to capture users' attitudes, goals, and pain points, aspects which analytics alone can't provide.

/videos/automating-research/.title: Automate Admin Tasks in the Research Process
/videos/automating-research/.summary: Conducting user research includes a lot of overhead and busy work. Find ways to streamline the process by automating repetitive administrative tasks using webhooks.

/videos/focus-groups/.title: Focus Groups 101
/videos/focus-groups/.summary: Focus groups are a polarizing research method. Within UX, they are best used in early discovery research to understand interest in a concept.

/videos/how-many-dots/.title: Dot Voting: How Many Dots?
/videos/how-many-dots/.summary: Use a simple equation or an absolute-number approach to decide how many dots to allocate in dot-voting activities. In most cases, 3-6 dots is appropriate.

/videos/personal-growth/.title: Personal Growth in UX: 5 Signs
/videos/personal-growth/.summary: There are five primary signs of personal growth in the UX field: gaining new skills, recognition from others, taking on strategic efforts, autonomy from leadership, and gaining confidence.

/videos/ideation-mindset/.title: Ideation is a Mindset
/videos/ideation-mindset/.summary: If you understand how to ideate well, you can always find ways to incorporate this process into your work.

/videos/selection-bias/.title: Selection Bias in UX Research
/videos/selection-bias/.summary: Every research study has bias, but you can curate and prioritize certain biases to address the questions that are important to you.

/videos/passwordless-accounts/.title: Passwordless Accounts
/videos/passwordless-accounts/.summary: A new pattern allows users to create an account without defining a password. Later on, they can log in through an OTP or a passkey.

/videos/stakeholder-interviews-101/.title: Stakeholder Interviews 101
/videos/stakeholder-interviews-101/.summary: UX-stakeholder interviews help us gather any information that may help shape the design process, define success metrics, and ultimately meet stakeholder expectations.

/videos/resumes-things-to-remove/.title: UX Resumes: 10 Things to Remove
/videos/resumes-things-to-remove/.summary: Supercharge your UX resume’s effectiveness by prioritizing substance over style, reducing bias, and highlighting results.

/videos/solo-researcher-grow/.title: The Solo UX Researcher: How to Grow
/videos/solo-researcher-grow/.summary: Dr. Jakob Nielsen answers the audience question "As the only UX researcher on my team, how do I learn and grow?"

/videos/accessibility-vs-inclusive-desig.title: Accessibility vs. Inclusive Design
/videos/accessibility-vs-inclusive-desig.summary: "Accessible design" and "inclusive design" are often used interchangeably. While they are related, their focuses are different.

/videos/sensitive-data/.title: Collecting Sensitive Demographic Data
/videos/sensitive-data/.summary: Demographic questions related to age, race, gender and income can be sensitive topics for research participants and need to be carefully framed by UX researchers.

/videos/design-sprints/.title: UX in Design Sprints
/videos/design-sprints/.summary: Learn how UX practitioners can lead in Design Sprints, especially with mapping, sketching, prototyping, and user research to enhance collaborative problem-solving.

/videos/independent-and-dependent-variab.title: Independent and Dependent Variables: Increase Impact with Small Changes
/videos/independent-and-dependent-variab.summary: Learn how to structure your research with independent and dependent variables to increase the clarity and impact of your work.

/videos/resolve-conflict/.title: Resolve Conflict in UX: 3 Steps
/videos/resolve-conflict/.summary: Overcoming conflict with product team partners has the potential to catalyze positive change. Start by diagnosing the issue, applying empathy, and focusing energy where you have influence.

/videos/accordions-on-mobile/.title: Accordions on Mobile
/videos/accordions-on-mobile/.summary: Accordions provide an overview of the whole page and mitigate the problem of long mobile pages, allowing users to directly access the content of interest.

/videos/designer-gatherings/.title: Designer Gatherings
/videos/designer-gatherings/.summary: Designer gatherings enable designers to share knowledge and helpful resources across an organization. Set up recurring designer gatherings to empower your design team.

/videos/engagement-metrics/.title: Engagement Metrics in UX
/videos/engagement-metrics/.summary: Engagement is an abstract, complex concept used to understand how much people interact with our products. Choosing the right engagement metrics goes beyond time spent.

/videos/gain-loss-framing/.title: Gain-Loss Framing
/videos/gain-loss-framing/.summary: Gain-loss framing in UX storytelling tailors arguments by emphasizing advantages or disadvantages of viewpoints.

/videos/primacy-effect/.title: Primacy Effect: Put Important Things First
/videos/primacy-effect/.summary: The primacy effect influences how user perceive and remember your designs. Learn how to work with it to create more effective experiences.

/videos/resumes-ux-career-changers/.title: Awesome Resumes for UX Career Changers
/videos/resumes-ux-career-changers/.summary: Changing your career into user experience? Reduce stress and improve your job prospects by redesigning your resume to emphasize your UX education and job-transferrable skills.

/videos/when-thinking-aloud-fails/.title: When Thinking Aloud Fails
/videos/when-thinking-aloud-fails/.summary: To understand the needs of work-domain experts, use retrospective testing, expert walkthroughs, and interviews instead of think-aloud usability-testing studies.

/videos/support-international-purchasers.title: 4 Ways to Support International Purchasers
/videos/support-international-purchasers.summary: Multiple support channels help global purchasers shop on your site smoothly and confidently. Choose at least two of the following: live chat, email, telephone, and social media.

/videos/why-hire-ux-generalists/.title: Why You Should Hire UX Generalists First
/videos/why-hire-ux-generalists/.summary: When building a UX team, start by hiring 2-3 UX generalists with complementary skill sets. This approach will allow the team to meet several needs of the organization and learn from each other.

/videos/ux-in-safe/.title: UX in SAFe
/videos/ux-in-safe/.summary: Learn 5 tips for how UX professionals can navigate and excel within the SAFe Agile framework.

/videos/visual-design-hacks/.title: Visual Design Hacks for the Non-designer
/videos/visual-design-hacks/.summary: Make your work look visually compelling by using these visual-design hacks: preexisting color palettes, cohesive icons, and grids for alignment.

/videos/level-up-focus-groups/.title: Level Up Your Focus Groups
/videos/level-up-focus-groups/.summary: To avoid common issues with focus groups, consider using these strategies to maximize participation and minimize the potential for bias.

/videos/inductively-analyzing-qualitativ.title: Inductively Analyzing Qualitative Data
/videos/inductively-analyzing-qualitativ.summary: Inductive analysis begins with no framework in mind and looks for naturally emerging patterns in the data.

/videos/contrast-charts/.title: Contrast in Charts
/videos/contrast-charts/.summary: Use color, titles, and callouts to draw your viewers' attention to the main finding in your quantitative-data visualization.

/videos/analytics-in-ux/.title: How to Use Analytics in UX
/videos/analytics-in-ux/.summary: Integrating analytics into UX work helps make data-based decisions and focuses effort on projects with the most impact.

/videos/balance-in-ux-design/.title: Balance in UX Design: Symmetry, Asymmetry, and Radial Balance
/videos/balance-in-ux-design/.summary: The kind of balance you use in your visual depends on what you want to convey. Symmetry is quiet and static. Asymmetry creates energy and movement. Radial balance leads attention to the central point.

/videos/research-goals-questions-hypothe.title: What, When, Why: Research Goals, Questions, and Hypotheses
/videos/research-goals-questions-hypothe.summary: Research questions, research goals, and hypotheses are 3 devices used to focus user research studies.

/videos/consistency-vs-innovation/.title: Consistency vs. Innovation in UX Design
/videos/consistency-vs-innovation/.summary: Any type of innovation requires users to learn the new pattern. It's worth departing from convention only if you are sure that the new pattern will perform better than what is already available.

/videos/cognitive-walkthroughs/.title: Cognitive Walkthroughs Help Assess Interface Learnability
/videos/cognitive-walkthroughs/.summary: A cognitive walkthrough is a task-based usability-inspection technique used to evaluate the learnability of a system from the perspective of a new user.

/videos/visual-design-ux-maps/.title: Visual Design of UX Maps
/videos/visual-design-ux-maps/.summary: Don’t make a UX map pretty for the sake of making it pretty. Invest in creating a visual system for your map then testing it and getting feedback.

/videos/visual-treatments-accessibility/.title: Visual Treatments that Improve Accessibility
/videos/visual-treatments-accessibility/.summary: To design accessible visuals, account for color contrast, don’t rely on color alone, and make interactive elements easy to identify.

/videos/lean-ux/.title: What is Lean UX?
/videos/lean-ux/.summary: Lean UX is a collaborative, crossfunctional design approach that establishes the true nature of a product in a fast, user-centered way.

/videos/users-real-data/.title: Usability Testing with Users' Personal Information
/videos/users-real-data/.summary: Usability Testing benefits from using participants’ personal information, but asking for this requires preparation and consideration.

/videos/chartjunk/.title: Clutter-Free Charts
/videos/chartjunk/.summary: Clear out chartjunk (unnecessary visual elements) for a more minimalist and understandable data visualization.

/videos/deductive-analysis/.title: Deductively Analyzing Qualitative Data
/videos/deductive-analysis/.summary: Deductive analysis begins with a framework in mind and makes sense of the data through that lens.

/videos/visual-weight/.title: What is Visual Weight?
/videos/visual-weight/.summary: Visual weight measures how much design elements draw attention from the viewer. Objects that are bigger in size, simpler in shape, use dark colors, or have high contrast appear visually heavier.

/videos/discovery-in-agile/.title: Discovery in Agile
/videos/discovery-in-agile/.summary: Scale discovery activities in agile projects; don't skip them. Five tips for ensuring the continuation of discovery research, regardless of the length of your sprints.

/videos/campbells-law/.title: Campbell's Law: The Dark Side of Success Metrics
/videos/campbells-law/.summary: When organizations optimize metrics at the cost of all else, they expose themselves to metric corruption, which can have disastrous consequences.

/videos/user-quotes/.title: Using Quotes to Share UX Research: 3 Tips
/videos/user-quotes/.summary: User quotes can be powerful and persuasive when sharing UX research insights, but most quotes need a little attention first.

/videos/using-empathy-maps/.title: How to Use Empathy Maps
/videos/using-empathy-maps/.summary: The empathy-mapping process helps distill and categorize knowledge of the user into one place, while the artifact serves as quick, digestible way to illustrate user attitudes and behaviors.

/videos/why-prioritize-personas/.title: Why Prioritize Personas?
/videos/why-prioritize-personas/.summary: Prioritizing your personas helps you make strategic design tradeoffs to ensure designs bring the most value to the business.

/videos/pilot-testing/.title: Pilot Testing in UX Research
/videos/pilot-testing/.summary: Pilot testing involves conducting one or two test sessions to evaluate the design of a usability study. It checks for any issues before the actual testing phase, leading to more reliable results.

/videos/long-tail/.title: Long-Tail Data in UX
/videos/long-tail/.summary: The long tail refers to the data points at the trailing end of a power-law distribution. A long-tail strategy involves efficiently exploiting these low-impact data points for an aggregated benefit.

/videos/choosing-chart-types/.title: Choosing Chart Types
/videos/choosing-chart-types/.summary: Pick a chart type that will help you make your point. In the vast majority of cases, use bar charts, line charts, or scatterplots.

/videos/choosing-color-palette/.title: Choosing a Color Palette
/videos/choosing-color-palette/.summary: Colors in an effective color palette work together, follow your brand’s color guidelines, and avoid overwhelming users.

/videos/usability-test-mistakes/.title: Usability Test Facilitation: 6 Mistakes to Avoid
/videos/usability-test-mistakes/.summary: Become a better usability testing facilitator by avoiding common missteps, like asking leading questions or reacting to user behavior.

/videos/informed-consent/.title: Informed Consent for UX Research
/videos/informed-consent/.summary: Ethically sound UX research requires informed consent from a research participant. Informed consent means the participant fully understands what the study entails and the potential consequences of participating.

/videos/proto-personas/.title: Proto Personas
/videos/proto-personas/.summary: Proto personas capture a team's existing knowledge or assumptions about who their current users are. These should be used with caution because they are created with no new research.

/videos/basic-psychology/.title: Basic Psychology Is Essential for UX Practitioners
/videos/basic-psychology/.summary: Basic psychological principles can guide you as a UX designer because most users share many common characteristics. Consider learning more about: motivation, attention, memory, persuasion, learning, decision making, emotion, sensation, perception, or cognitive biases.

/videos/hire-retain-ux-employees/.title: Hire and Retain UX Employees
/videos/hire-retain-ux-employees/.summary: Hiring for attitude, training for skill, and planning before posting job descriptions helps UX managers hire and retain the right UX talent.

/videos/think-aloud/.title: Help Users Think Aloud
/videos/think-aloud/.summary: Help users think aloud by explaining what it is and why it's useful, reinforcing the behavior, and prompting along the way.

/videos/confounding-variables-deal-with-.title: Confounding Variables: How to Deal with Them (Part 2 of 2)
/videos/confounding-variables-deal-with-.summary: Confounding variables can be the result of a variety of factors, but following best practices can help avoid most of them.

/videos/problem-solution-space/.title: Problem Space and Solution Space Research
/videos/problem-solution-space/.summary: Both problem-space and solution-space research are needed to design products that are useful and usable.

/videos/product-partners/.title: Collaborating with Product Partners: 3 Tips
/videos/product-partners/.summary: Team up with product partners more effectively by making research accessible, framing the context and value of analytics, and establishing a regular communication cadence.

/videos/language-switchers/.title: 6 Tips for Improving Language Switchers on Ecommerce Sites
/videos/language-switchers/.summary: International purchasers are more comfortable shopping in their own language.  Follow these tips to make the language switcher on your site more discoverable and usable.

/videos/content-inventory-audit/.title: How To: Content Inventory and Audit
/videos/content-inventory-audit/.summary: Content inventories and audits shift a team's mindset from content quantity to content quality. They reveal relationships between content to resolve problems and support new content creation.

/videos/hybrid-workshops/.title: Running Workshops with Both Remote and In-Person Participants
/videos/hybrid-workshops/.summary: Hybrid workshops are the ultimate test of facilitation skills: you must bridge the gap between in-person and remote participants, not widen the divide. There are three types of hybrid workshops and each presents its own set of logistical nightmares.

/videos/confounding-variables-1/.title: Confounding Variables 101 (Part 1 of 2)
/videos/confounding-variables-1/.summary: Confounding variables can affect the validity of data collected during research studies. It's important for researchers to know what they are and how to identify them.

/videos/onboarding-new-hires/.title: Onboarding New UX Hires: 3 Tips
/videos/onboarding-new-hires/.summary: Improve your new UX hires' onboarding experience by auditing the current experience, making thoughtful interactions, and creating a 30/60/90-day plan.

/videos/downsides-net-promoter-score/.title: Downsides of the Net Promoter Score
/videos/downsides-net-promoter-score/.summary: The Net Promoter Score (NPS) can be gamed, and its definition loses information and precision by treating fairly dissimilar responses in the same way. It should be used together with other UX metrics rather than in isolation.

/videos/ux-vision-strategy-questions/.title: UX Vision & Strategy: Top Questions Answered
/videos/ux-vision-strategy-questions/.summary: A UX vision is a part of a UX strategy, alongside goals (or measures) and a plan.

/videos/democratization-of-ux/.title: Democratization of UX
/videos/democratization-of-ux/.summary: Democratization of UX work, or making it acceptable and accessible for everyone, must be accompanied by due diligence: setting guidelines, educating others, and demystifying the process.

/videos/product-instrumentation/.title: Product Instrumentation: 3 Benefits
/videos/product-instrumentation/.summary: Product instrumentation tells us when and how much people use different aspects of our product. This insight can inform feature prioritization, validate our assumptions, and identify potential user problems.

/videos/building-rapport/.title: Building Rapport with UX Research Participants
/videos/building-rapport/.summary: Researchers should build rapport and embrace real human interactions to put participants at ease during a study.

/videos/when-to-empathy-map/.title: When to Empathy Map
/videos/when-to-empathy-map/.summary: Empathy maps can be used to plan for future research studies, capture insights during current user research, and communicate research insights from research that has already been conducted.

/videos/prototype-specifications/.title: Prototype Specifications: 3 Types
/videos/prototype-specifications/.summary: Element, functionality, and content are three types of prototype specifications that help us document design details that are otherwise easily overlooked.

/videos/ux-research-roadmaps/.title: UX Research Roadmaps
/videos/ux-research-roadmaps/.summary: A UX research roadmap is a living artifact that prioritizes and communicates a team’s future research efforts, from early discovery-based initiatives to later-stage usability testing.

/videos/protecting-participant-data/.title: Protecting Participant Data: 6 Best Practices
/videos/protecting-participant-data/.summary: Research participants are more vulnerable than ever as researchers conduct remote usability tests, use third-party applications, and store data online. Protect participant privacy by adhering to best practices before, during, and after data collection.

/videos/system-usability-scale/.title: The System Usability Scale (SUS)
/videos/system-usability-scale/.summary: The SUS is a well-established 10-question survey administered at the end of a user test; it gives you a measure of the perceived usability of your product and enables you to compare it with others.

/videos/discovery-kick-off-workshops/.title: Discovery Kick Off Workshops
/videos/discovery-kick-off-workshops/.summary: Starting discovery with a structured kick off workshop can create alignment and set your discovery efforts up for success.

/videos/impact-on-ux/.title: Impact on UX: Individual Designers vs. Systematic Methodology
/videos/impact-on-ux/.summary: How is the quality of the final design impacted by the contribution of individual designers vs. the outcome of following systematic UX methodology?

/videos/information-architecture-models/.title: Information Architecture: 3 Key Models
/videos/information-architecture-models/.summary: Navigation, taxonomies, and the full IA structure are different ways of modeling a product's structure. We review the differences and similarities between these three different IA models.

/videos/il1-typography-test/.title: The IL1 Typography Test
/videos/il1-typography-test/.summary: Using typefaces with distinct characters can help users easily differentiate alphanumeric data. Choose typefaces that pass the I-L-1 test for data tables and information seen at-a-glance.

/videos/ux-of-phone-trees/.title: The UX of Phone Trees
/videos/ux-of-phone-trees/.summary: Phone trees are notoriously frustrating for 4 main reasons. There are many small ways to make them more usable and less miserable, however.

/videos/usability-101/.title: Usability 101
/videos/usability-101/.summary: Usability assesses how easy user interfaces are to use. Usability is defined by 5 quality components: learnability, efficiency, memorability, errors, and satisfaction.

/videos/tips-for-new-prototypers/.title: 5 Tips for New Prototypers
/videos/tips-for-new-prototypers/.summary: Are you new to prototyping? We compiled our favorite design and workflow tips to help you create effective prototypes for usability testing.

/videos/discount-usability-revisited/.title: Discount Usability Revisited (Jakob Nielsen Keynote)
/videos/discount-usability-revisited/.summary: 3 methods for cheap and fast UX work are still good advice to emphasize iterative design and accelerate UX maturity improvements (This was Jakob Nielsen's keynote at the in-person Washington DC UX Conference)

/videos/better-hiring-interviews/.title: How to Conduct Better Hiring Interviews for UX Teams
/videos/better-hiring-interviews/.summary: Job interviews are usually terrible at predicting future performance. Learn how structuring your hiring interviews can help UX teams strike gold by identifying high-performing and diverse hires with a less biased process.

/videos/how-much-ux/.title: How Much UX Do You Need?
/videos/how-much-ux/.summary: Spend more on UX design projects that have a higher risk of failure from bad design or a higher payoff from great design.

/videos/introducing-a-usability-test/.title: Introducing a Participant to a Usability Test: A Demonstration
/videos/introducing-a-usability-test/.summary: Facilitation experts demonstrate how to prepare a participant for the test session. Use a facilitator’s script to help remember the important information that participants need to know.

/videos/ux-stakeholder-engagement-101/.title: UX Stakeholder Engagement 101
/videos/ux-stakeholder-engagement-101/.summary: Engaging with stakeholders is a requirement if we want to ship great experiences. It should be integrated with your team’s routines, tools, and methods — so that it feels sustainable and effective.

/videos/common-region-gestalt/.title: Common Region: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/common-region-gestalt/.summary: Items within a boundary are perceived as a group and assumed to share some common characteristic or functionality.

/videos/funnel-technique-interviews/.title: Using the Funnel Technique in User Interviews
/videos/funnel-technique-interviews/.summary: Start with broad, open-ended questions in your interviews before introducing more specific questions to gather accurate, in-depth information.

/videos/common-antipersonas/.title: 3 Common Antipersonas in UX
/videos/common-antipersonas/.summary: Considering 3 main antipersonas in your design process can prevent much misuse or other grief which would undermine the user experience after the product is released.

/videos/prospective-students/.title: What Every Prospective University Student Wants to Know
/videos/prospective-students/.summary: Most prospective university students have four main questions, but choosing which schools to apply to is a very challenging process for them.

/videos/users-you-have/.title: You Have the Users You Have
/videos/users-you-have/.summary: The only realistic design strategy is to cater to the actual people who use your product, instead of designing for an idealized super-user who knows more and is more motivated than the real audience.

/videos/alternatives-to-infinite-scrolli.title: 3 Alternatives to Infinite Scrolling
/videos/alternatives-to-infinite-scrolli.summary: Infinite scrolling can create great user experiences, but it also has weaknesses. Consider 3 alternative design patterns that may work better for your product: A load-more button, integrated pagination within a long scroll, and traditional pages.

/videos/figure-ground-gestalt/.title: Figure/Ground: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/figure-ground-gestalt/.summary: Users perceive interface design elements that differentiate the foreground (figure) from the background (ground) as something to focus on or interact with.

/videos/important-work-startup/.title: The Most Important Work for the UX Team in a Startup Company
/videos/important-work-startup/.summary: In a startup company, the UX team can make two main contributions: identifying the customer problem to solve and polishing the UI so that people will use this solution.

/videos/building-trust-ux/.title: Building Trust in UX
/videos/building-trust-ux/.summary: Whether UX succeeds or fails comes down to whether other people in the organization trust the UX team, the UX process, and the UX findings and designs. Low trust = poor outcomes, no matter how good the work, so building trust is a priority.

/videos/clarify-dont-mystify/.title: Clarify, Don't Mystify (UX Slogan #19)
/videos/clarify-dont-mystify/.summary: UX design must make all elements of the interaction understandable and explicit. Mystifying things to entice more clicks from users will only result in dissatisfied customers.

/videos/unmanned-restaurants/.title: The User Experience of Unmanned Restaurants in China
/videos/unmanned-restaurants/.summary: Our Beijing-based user research team conducted a field study in automated restaurants that serve diners with no staff. Current designs have some advantages, but the UI is too complicated for customized ordering.

/videos/content-strategy-101/.title: Content Strategy 101
/videos/content-strategy-101/.summary: Content involves 4 phases: planning, creation, maintenance, and removal. Done right, this enhances the business value of digital content and its impact on the user experience.

/videos/continuation-gestalt/.title: Continuation: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/continuation-gestalt/.summary: The eye automatically follows lines and curves, continuing them. Employ continuation to guide users along desired paths in the UI.

/videos/pareto-principle/.title: Focus Your Design Tactics with the Pareto Principle
/videos/pareto-principle/.summary: A small share of all items produce most of the impact: a few features, a few usability problems, a few customers, and your key persona. Focusing design efforts on those high-impact areas leads to higher success rather than broadly (and thinly) distributed UX work.

/videos/40-years/.title: 40 Years in UX
/videos/40-years/.summary: Jakob Nielsen on what has changed and what has remained the same since he started in UX in 1983.

/videos/funnel-usability-testing/.title: Using the Funnel Technique in Usability Testing
/videos/funnel-usability-testing/.summary: Even when you want to test a specific feature, start with broader tasks to capture natural user behavior and observe what participants would do on their own. If they fail, follow up with directed tasks.

/videos/ux-strategy-components/.title: UX Strategy Components
/videos/ux-strategy-components/.summary: Each component of a UX strategy plays an important role in helping teams work toward a better future state of the experience by aligning user needs with business priorities.

/videos/common-fate-gestalt/.title: Common Fate: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/common-fate-gestalt/.summary: Things that move in synch are perceived as belonging to the same group and being different than other screen elements that stay put or move differently.

/videos/community-ecommerce/.title: Community Ecommerce
/videos/community-ecommerce/.summary: Ecommerce user experience can benefit from community features. Our user research in China finds that shoppers often view such content as more credible and useful than brand content.

/videos/antipersonas/.title: Antipersonas in UX
/videos/antipersonas/.summary: Antipersonas represent people who could misuse your product in ways that negatively impact target users and the business. Formalizing a description of the 8 aspects of an antipersonas can help a design team mitigate such risks.

/videos/stop-solutioneering/.title: Stop Solutioneering (UX Slogan # 18)
/videos/stop-solutioneering/.summary: UX designers and engineering teams are often too quick to propose solutions, without understanding the problem (or even if there is a problem at all). Ask questions first, before jumping to a solution.

/videos/infinite-scrolling-when/.title: Infinite Scrolling: When to Use It, When to Avoid It
/videos/infinite-scrolling-when/.summary: Infinite scrolling through long lists of homogeneous items can lower interaction costs, but is less suited to support specific tasks such as finding a particular item.

/videos/too-easy/.title: This Is Too Easy to Understand (UX Slogan #17)
/videos/too-easy/.summary: User interfaces can definitely be too hard to use, but can they be too easy? No, users never complain about an easy design, even if they would have been able to use something more difficult.

/videos/connectedness-gestalt/.title: Connectedness: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/connectedness-gestalt/.summary: Visual design elements that are connected (for example, by a line) are seen as belonging together. This principle is strong enough to overrule small differences between the items.

/videos/not-all-ux-trends/.title: Not All UX Trends Are Right for You
/videos/not-all-ux-trends/.summary: It can be tempting to follow the next big UX trend. Before adopting a UX trend, we must evaluate how the trend will support users and impact our workflows.

/videos/it-depends-ux-slogan-14/.title: It Depends (UX Slogan #14)
/videos/it-depends-ux-slogan-14/.summary: UX design is hyper-multidimensional, with many conflicting criteria and a highly context-dependent decision process.

/videos/ux-internships/.title: UX Internships
/videos/ux-internships/.summary: Advice for students in user-experience programs on what to look for in a UX internship.

/videos/closure-gestalt/.title: Closure: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/closure-gestalt/.summary: People often fill in the gaps between visual elements, using closure to perceive them as a whole instead of being separate UI items.

/videos/alert-fatigue-user-interfaces/.title: Alert Fatigue in User Interfaces
/videos/alert-fatigue-user-interfaces/.summary: Dashboards that monitor vast masses of data should guide users' attention to critical values but not by flashing endless alerts without prioritization.

/videos/metaverse-ux/.title: The Metaverse and User Experience
/videos/metaverse-ux/.summary: Metaverse projects must follow the standard user-centered design process, including prototyping and usability testing, to result in useful designs that people will want to use.

/videos/checklist-for-moderating-user-te.title: Checklist for Moderating a User Test
/videos/checklist-for-moderating-user-te.summary: 10 things you should do when running a usability study. Remembering all the steps leads to good research insights. (The second of 2 videos on usability study checklists.)

/videos/internal-vs-external-validity-ux.title: Internal vs. External Validity in UX-Study Design
/videos/internal-vs-external-validity-ux.summary: Internal validity ensures that your study design does not favor any particular condition or response, while external validity is about a naturalistic study setup and choice of participants.

/videos/users-are-not-lazy/.title: Users Are Not Lazy (UX Slogan #10)
/videos/users-are-not-lazy/.summary: Users don't work hard enough to discover how to use your design in the intended manner. Bad user! But really, they're just prioritizing their own time and interests and behaving the way evolution made people.

/videos/proximity-gestalt/.title: Proximity: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
/videos/proximity-gestalt/.summary: UI elements that are close together are perceived as belonging together, whereas users think that things that are apart play different roles in the interaction.

/videos/show-me-the-data/.title: Show Me the Data (UX Slogan #15)
/videos/show-me-the-data/.summary: Members of a design team will often argue for different solutions to a UI problem. That's when to say "show me the data" to resolve the debate by empirical insights, rather than who argues the best.

/videos/where-should-designops-focus/.title: Where Should DesignOps Focus?
/videos/where-should-designops-focus/.summary: What's most useful in building a DesignOps program depends on the level of maturity in the specific organization. In the beginning, focus on pain points. Later, focus on building scale.

/videos/augmented-reality-calibration/.title: 5 Tips for Augmented Reality Calibration
/videos/augmented-reality-calibration/.summary: Before users can use an AR app, they must often calibrate it first. Usability studies find many big problems in calibration designs that can prevent people from ever getting into the actual AR experience.

/videos/checklist-planning-user-test/.title: Checklist for Planning a User Test
/videos/checklist-planning-user-test/.summary: 10 things you should do *before* you actually run a usability study. Good planning leads to good research insights. (The first of 2 videos on usability study checklists.)

/videos/get-helpful-feedback/.title: How to Get Helpful Feedback
/videos/get-helpful-feedback/.summary: To get useful feedback on UX design or research, set the stage with stakeholders before presenting the work. Provide context and deliberately ask for the types of feedback that will be most helpful to you.

/videos/we-like-to-watch/.title: UX Researchers, We Like to Watch (UX Slogan #16)
/videos/we-like-to-watch/.summary: Watching users' actual behavior helps us gain insights to improve the user experience.

/videos/make-it-easy-ux-slogan-8/.title: Make It Easy (UX Slogan #8)
/videos/make-it-easy-ux-slogan-8/.summary: It's hard work to make a user interface that's easy to use. The end result may seem obvious to an outsider, but ease-of-use comes from trying out many design ideas and rejecting ones that are too difficult while polishing those that make the UI better.

/videos/six-levels-of-ux-maturity/.title: Six Levels of UX Maturity
/videos/six-levels-of-ux-maturity/.summary: Organizations may progress through 6 levels of UX Maturity, from "absent" to "user-driven".

/videos/secondary-research-important-ux-.title: Secondary Research: Important UX Learning Right at Your Desk
/videos/secondary-research-important-ux-.summary: You don't have to do all UX research yourself. You should learn from existing published work, which will save you much time, especially when beginning a new project.

/videos/screen-your-research-participant.title: Screen Your Research Participants to Avoid Bias in User Research
/videos/screen-your-research-participant.summary: Rule #1 for all user research is to study participants who are representative of the target audience. 5 best practices for recruiting screeners will improve the validity of your research.

/videos/should-designops-be-a-dedicated-.title: Should DesignOps Be a Dedicated Role?
/videos/should-designops-be-a-dedicated-.summary: DesignOps can be a dedicated role or a shared responsibility. Regardless of approach, make sure to benchmark and track related initiatives over time to continue securing buy-in for DesignOps efforts.

/videos/similarity-gestalt-principle/.title: Similarity: Gestalt Principle 1 for UI Design
/videos/similarity-gestalt-principle/.summary: User interface elements that share one or more traits (such as shape, color, size, etc.) will be seen by users as being similar and belonging together.

/videos/the-gestalt-principles-intro/.title: The Gestalt Principles for User Interface Design
/videos/the-gestalt-principles-intro/.summary: The gestalt principles for visual perception make users see some graphical user interface design elements as parts of a whole, and others as being separate, and thus different.

/videos/managing-visual-complexity/.title: 3 Strategies for Managing Visual Complexity in Applications and Websites
/videos/managing-visual-complexity/.summary: In application design, prevent users from being overwhelmed by putting things in predictable places, using a clear visual hierarchy, and taking advantage of progressive disclosure.

/videos/matrix-reporting/.title: UX Researchers Reporting Structure
/videos/matrix-reporting/.summary: Our recent survey of UXers shows that researchers report in a matrix style. Matrix offers benefits from both a central research team and product teams.

/videos/explain-ux-user-centered-design/.title: Explain UX with User-Centered Design
/videos/explain-ux-user-centered-design/.summary: Most short explanations of "what is UX?" are quite internally-focused and rely on understanding the process for building digital products. Here are 3 steps to explain what you do that normal people can understand and will relate to.

/videos/ux-is-people-ux-slogan-7/.title: UX Is People (UX Slogan #7)
/videos/ux-is-people-ux-slogan-7/.summary: User experience is not really about computers or technology. It's about the users (people) and about the design teams and proper processes for their members (people) to produce good UX.

/videos/design-for-them/.title: Design for Them Not for You (UX Slogan #13)
/videos/design-for-them/.summary: It does not matter whether you like a design or whether you find the product easy to use. We must design for the way real customers actually behave.

/videos/empty-states-in-application-desi.title: Empty States in Application Design: 3 Guidelines
/videos/empty-states-in-application-desi.summary: Well-designed empty states in applications can help increase user confidence, improve system learnability, and help users get started with key tasks quickly.

/videos/strategic-reactionary-user-resea.title: Strategic & Reactionary User Research
/videos/strategic-reactionary-user-resea.summary: User research is often initiated during a sprint, after a design is implemented, or is part of the MVP. But, mindfully planning research earlier reaps far better results.

/videos/five-prioritization-methods/.title: UX Design Prioritization Methods
/videos/five-prioritization-methods/.summary: You cannot do everything, and in fact the product would be worse if it included everything. Thus, UX relies heavily on prioritization to determine what features add the most value relative to the resources needed to deliver them.

/videos/vertical-navigation/.title: Vertical Navigation
/videos/vertical-navigation/.summary: Websites with many categories can benefit from showing navigation menu options in a vertical list: vertical menus allow for easy expansion, are easy to scan, plus users are familiar with this design pattern.

/videos/why-ux-keynote/.title: Why UX?
/videos/why-ux-keynote/.summary: Key arguments why companies should have systematic user-experience processes. Plus a discussion of the main arguments against UX. (Jakob Nielsen's UX Conference keynote.)

/videos/visual-hierarchy/.title: Visual Hierarchy
/videos/visual-hierarchy/.summary: Visual hierarchy can help users decide where to look in a user interface: what's most important can be shown by color and size, and what things belong together can be shown by proximity and common regions.

/videos/types-of-user-pain-points/.title: Types of User Pain Points
/videos/types-of-user-pain-points/.summary: Problems with a customer's experience can be big or small and fall into 3 categories: interaction level, journey level, and relationship level. UX resources should be prioritized to find and fix the most painful issues.

/videos/audience-based-website-navigatio.title: Audience-Based Website Navigation
/videos/audience-based-website-navigatio.summary: Segmenting a website's navigation by audience categories will often degrade usability, either because users belong in multiple categories, or because they feel the need to look at content targeted at several segments.

/videos/number-one-reason-for-not-doing-.title: The Number One Reason for Not Doing UX Research
