/videos/number-one-reason-for-not-doing-.summary: Barriers from all angles can make doing user research seem impossible. But recognizing the challenges and knowing you are not alone in having them, makes them easier to overcome so that you can get user data after all.

/videos/why-beats-what-ux-slogan-6/.title: "Why" Beats "What" in UX (UX Slogan #6)
/videos/why-beats-what-ux-slogan-6/.summary: Data about what users do is valuable, but not nearly as valuable as information about why people did something. Such "why" insight should drive UX design decisions.

/videos/how-many-users-contextual-inquir.title: How Many Users Should You Visit for Contextual Inquiry?
/videos/how-many-users-contextual-inquir.summary: The question of "how many users" has 3 answers when doing contextual inquiry: users per visit, visits per day, and the total number of visits in a study (which again varies depending on the type of design project).

/videos/more-choices-more-trouble-ux-slo.title: More Choices More Trouble (UX Slogan #12)
/videos/more-choices-more-trouble-ux-slo.summary: The more choices a user has to make, the bigger the risk of getting into trouble. More features can easily reduce usability.

/videos/ab-testing-roadmap/.title: A/B Testing Roadmap
/videos/ab-testing-roadmap/.summary: 6 steps to consider when planning a systematic set of A/B tests to optimize a design for the long haul.

/videos/simplest-way-to-get-buy-in-for-u.title: The Simplest Way to Get Buy-In for UX
/videos/simplest-way-to-get-buy-in-for-u.summary: Understand motivations and try different approaches to get stakeholder buy-in for UX research, findings, and design recommendations.

/videos/what-is-journey-management/.title: What Is Journey Management?
/videos/what-is-journey-management/.summary: User journeys should be managed like products — by people and teams with specialized, journey-dedicated roles who continually research, measure, optimize, and orchestrate the experience.

/videos/tips-bulleted-lists-digital-cont.title: 4 Tips for Bulleted Lists in Digital Content
/videos/tips-bulleted-lists-digital-cont.summary: Bulleted lists can save users time and help them scan our content more quickly, but only when they’re used correctly.

/videos/ux-roadmaps-common-questions/.title: UX Roadmaps Common Questions
/videos/ux-roadmaps-common-questions/.summary: 5 questions we often get asked in the course on UX roadmaps, starting with the difference between roadmaps and project plans.

/videos/test-5-users-qual-vs-quant/.title: 5 Users: Okay for Qual, Wrong for Quant
/videos/test-5-users-qual-vs-quant/.summary: The recommended sample size (the number of study participants) is very different for qualitative user testing (small N) and for quantitative research (big N). Here's why the recommendations differ.

/videos/five-ways-to-recruit-participant.title: Five Ways to Recruit Participants for User Research
/videos/five-ways-to-recruit-participant.summary: Getting representative members of the target audience as your test participants is essential for user research validity. You can outsource recruiting to an agency, or do it yourself. Each method has its own advantages and possible biases.

/videos/checking-guessing-ux-slogan/.title: If You're Not Checking, You're Guessing (UX Slogan #11)
/videos/checking-guessing-ux-slogan/.summary: Even the smallest amount of empirical findings about your target audience and their use of your UI will lead to vastly better design decisions than if you're designing without data. Because then you're just guessing.

/videos/emojis-email-subject-lines/.title: Should Emojis Be Used in Email Subject Lines?
/videos/emojis-email-subject-lines/.summary: We conducted user research to understand the impact of emojis in email subject lines. They can be useful once in a while, but should not be overused.

/videos/guided-vs-unguided-user-studies/.title: Guided vs. Unguided User Studies
/videos/guided-vs-unguided-user-studies/.summary: Directed user research where you ask people closed-end questions can bias the outcome in favor of those things that are being asked about. Unguided studies are often better at revealing true user preferences.

/videos/polyhierarchy-information-archit.title: Polyhierarchy in Information Architecture
/videos/polyhierarchy-information-archit.summary: Polyhierarchy is used to place a single item in more than one IA category. This can support users with different mental models but should be used judiciously.

/videos/3-myths-about-designops/.title: 3 Myths About DesignOps
/videos/3-myths-about-designops/.summary: Misconceptions stem from a lack of understanding of DesignOps, as well as attempts to pigeonhole it. DesignOps is different from design management, it's not always a specialized role, and it should be structured differently in different organizations.

/videos/collecting-ux-metrics-qualitativ.title: Collecting UX Metrics During Qualitative User Studies
/videos/collecting-ux-metrics-qualitativ.summary: Qualitative user research aims at insights, not numbers. Metrics for individual users help tell the story of how each person did, but mean values across a small sample won't be reliable.

/videos/brevity-brilliance-ux-slogan-5/.title: Brevity = Brilliance (UX Slogan #5)
/videos/brevity-brilliance-ux-slogan-5/.summary: The smaller the word count (and in general, the more concise your online communication), the more users will comprehend and retain your message.

/videos/why-remote-or-hybrid-workshops-f.title: Why Remote or Hybrid Workshops Fail
/videos/why-remote-or-hybrid-workshops-f.summary: Some of the biggest pitfalls in running remote or hybrid UX workshops come from poor choice of remote tools, poor agendas, or not managing expectations appropriately before the meeting.

/videos/progressive-disclosure/.title: Progressive Disclosure
/videos/progressive-disclosure/.summary: To reduce complexity in a user interface, employ progressive disclosure to defer secondary options to a subsidiary screen. This focuses users' attention on the primary options, which are the only ones shown by default.

/videos/using-personas-prioritize-featur.title: Using Personas to Prioritize Features
/videos/using-personas-prioritize-featur.summary: Put your personas to work by using them to evaluate and compare features and user stories to inform work priorities.

/videos/design-thinking-activities/.title: Design Thinking Activities
/videos/design-thinking-activities/.summary: The 6 stages of the design thinking process can be supported by a very wide range of UX methods and activities. Don't limit yourself to the most commonly mentioned methods.

/videos/writing-digital-copy-specialists.title: Writing Content for Generalists vs. Specialists
/videos/writing-digital-copy-specialists.summary: Content writers should always avoid jargon, but what counts as jargon depends on your audience. Determine whether a specific word is meaningless jargon or meaningful terminology.

/videos/long-waits-in-applications-guide.title: Designing for Long Waits in Applications: 3 Guidelines
/videos/long-waits-in-applications-guide.summary: 3 guidelines help mitigate the frustrations users often feel during long waits experienced in complex applications.

/videos/okrs-in-ux/.title: Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) in UX
/videos/okrs-in-ux/.summary: Define objectives and measurable key results to guide and track UX work. Use OKRs as a tool to align your team, provide focus, and a tangible way to monitor progress.

/videos/researchers-mindset/.title: A Researcher’s Mindset
/videos/researchers-mindset/.summary: There will never be firm rules for every detail of good user research, but cultivating a researcher's mindset will help you make sure that your research findings are valid.

/videos/using-color-enhance-design/.title: Using Color to Enhance Your Design
/videos/using-color-enhance-design/.summary: Color is an influential tool in user interface design. Here are 3 guidelines for applying color in your design.

/videos/communication-not-decoration-ux-.title: Communication Not Decoration (UX Slogan #4)
/videos/communication-not-decoration-ux-.summary: Users visit websites and use apps to get things done, so emphasize the content of interest to communicate with your audience. Avoid design pollution that decorates the UI with noncommunicative elements.

/videos/outcomes-over-outputs/.title: Outcomes Over Outputs
/videos/outcomes-over-outputs/.summary: Teams often fall into the trap of focusing on outputs (features, deliverables, and artifacts). Instead, a mindset shift of working toward purposeful outcomes (problems solved, needs addressed, and real benefits) leads to better results.

/videos/usability-testing-101/.title: Usability Testing 101
/videos/usability-testing-101/.summary: UX researchers use this popular method to uncover problems and opportunities in designs.

/videos/ux-progress-reports/.title: Weekly UX Progress Reports
/videos/ux-progress-reports/.summary: UX professionals should share user feedback and insights with team members from other disciplines early and often. Weekly UX progress reports keep findings and progress transparent without overloading people with too much information.

/videos/field-studies-vs-diary-studies/.title: Field Studies vs. Diary Studies
/videos/field-studies-vs-diary-studies/.summary: Field studies and diary studies are two research methods that help you learn about your users' real-world context, which is important for good design. They have different advantages and downsides.

/videos/why-ux-mentoring/.title: Why You Need UX Mentoring
/videos/why-ux-mentoring/.summary: Mentoring provides vocational support, psychological support, and role modeling, all of which can be particularly important in UX where many new professionals are on their own or have insufficient career support.

/videos/3-levels-emotional-processing/.title: The 3 Levels of Emotional Processing
/videos/3-levels-emotional-processing/.summary: People react user experience at 3 levels of emotional processing, as defined by Don Norman: visceral, behavioral, and reflective. Understanding these different levels is important for better UX design.

/videos/ux-roadmap-themes/.title: UX Roadmap Themes
/videos/ux-roadmap-themes/.summary: Instead of feature-focused roadmaps, theme-based UX roadmaps visualize experience strategy by communicating high-level opportunities and problems to solve. Include these 7 elements in each theme on the roadmap.

/videos/framing-ux-data-with-storytellin.title: Framing UX Data with Storytelling
/videos/framing-ux-data-with-storytellin.summary: For increased engagement and memorability, combine abstract UX data and statistics with anecdotes and metaphors to help your audience better visualize the numbers.

/videos/less-is-more-ux-slogan-9/.title: Less Is More (UX Slogan #9)
/videos/less-is-more-ux-slogan-9/.summary: If you can add more and more features and several different ways of doing a task, should you do so? No, more UI isn't more usability. Usually, less is more, so focus on users' key tasks and design simple interactions for each task.

/videos/journey-mapping-vs-story-mapping.title: Journey Mapping vs. Story Mapping
/videos/journey-mapping-vs-story-mapping.summary: How does a user story map differ from a customer journey map? A journey map is from the perspective of the person's experience, whereas a story map is from the perspective of the product and what it takes to deliver the user experience.

/videos/you-cant-impose-joy-ux-slogan-3/.title: You Can't Impose Joy (UX Slogan #3)
/videos/you-cant-impose-joy-ux-slogan-3/.summary: Some UX designers (and many clients) aim to "jazz up" the design to supposedly engage users. This usually backfires because extraneous design elements get in the way of users' tasks.

/videos/simple-clear-language-improves-u.title: Simple, Clear Language Improves UX
/videos/simple-clear-language-improves-u.summary: Complex content slows down users and distracts from task performance, thus degrading the user experience. Clear language facilitates comprehension. It's that simple.

/videos/this-vs-that-confusing-ux-terms/.title: This vs. That: Confusing UX Terms Compared
/videos/this-vs-that-confusing-ux-terms/.summary: User experience, user interface, customer experience, service design, usability: all these terms have simple definitions and cover related but different aspects of great design.

/videos/analytics-vs-quantitative-usabil.title: Analytics vs. Quantitative Usability Testing
/videos/analytics-vs-quantitative-usabil.summary: Both UX research techniques help you gain quantitative insight into user behavior. Each method provides different types of information and can answer different kinds of research questions, however.

/videos/great-ux-mentorship/.title: The C's of Great UX Mentorship
/videos/great-ux-mentorship/.summary: Both mentors and mentees need to put effort into the relationship: here are 3 traits for each side, plus 2 more that both should share.

/videos/designops-team-structures/.title: 5 DesignOps Team Structures
/videos/designops-team-structures/.summary: These 5 types of DesignOps team structures illustrate the varied approaches that can support and enable design organizations.

/videos/keep-it-simple-ux-slogan-2/.title: Keep It Simple (UX Slogan #2)
/videos/keep-it-simple-ux-slogan-2/.summary: The road to usability is paved with temptations to complicate the design with extra features and options, but resisting featuritis is the best prescription for a good user experience.

/videos/dont-be-scared-of-saying-i-dont-.title: Don’t Be Scared of Saying ‘I Don’t Know’
/videos/dont-be-scared-of-saying-i-dont-.summary: Saying 'I don't know' at work can be scary, but by focusing on how you would find the answer to the question, you'll still be in control of the conversation.

/videos/making-ux-research-goals-specifi.title: Making UX Research Goals Specific
/videos/making-ux-research-goals-specifi.summary: User research studies need research goals: what are you trying to learn? Too broad, and you may have no actionable insights to drive the design process.

/videos/interview-mistakes-to-avoid/.title: Five User Interview Mistakes to Avoid (in 5 Minutes)
/videos/interview-mistakes-to-avoid/.summary: Probing vs. leading. Saying enough to make your participant comfortable, but not so much you derail the research. 5 pitfalls in the user interview process are demonstrated so that you can avoid them the next time you talk with users.

/videos/user-story-mapping/.title: User Story Mapping 101
/videos/user-story-mapping/.summary: User story maps visualize the activities, steps, and details users go through in a product or feature. Instead of heavy requirements documents, story maps communicate how the pieces fit together before design and development.

/videos/stop-obsessing-over-features-foc.title: Stop Obsessing Over Features: Focus on User Goals to Solve Real Problems
/videos/stop-obsessing-over-features-foc.summary: Focusing on shipping new features instead of solving customer problems results in products and services that don't serve real users. Shift the mindset from 'what did we get done' to 'how valuable is the work that we're delivering' to avoid becoming a feature factory.

/videos/top-3-informational-interview-qu.title: Top 3 Informational Interview Questions in UX
/videos/top-3-informational-interview-qu.summary: Informational interviews allow you to connect with users and other people and get a glimpse into their world and how and why they work. They serve as an informal research tool for learning about a new domain or role.

/videos/design-thinking-top-3-challenges.title: Design Thinking: Top 3 Challenges and Solutions
/videos/design-thinking-top-3-challenges.summary: How to overcome 3 common challenges with design thinking: my team isn't interested, I have no time, I don't know where to start.

/videos/you-are-not-user-slogan/.title: You ≠ User (UX Slogan #1)
/videos/you-are-not-user-slogan/.summary: The foundation of user experience is the difference between the people on the design team and the people using the product. You can't ask users to design, but you also can't ask the designers whether their own design will be easy for the target audience to use.

/videos/3-uses-skill-mapping-ux-teams/.title: 3 Uses for Skill Mapping in UX Teams
/videos/3-uses-skill-mapping-ux-teams/.summary: Skill maps can be used to better understand team composition, identify the skills of new team members, and track career progression.

/videos/informal-organization-ux/.title: How Things Really Get Done in UX: The Informal Organization
/videos/informal-organization-ux/.summary: UX professionals often do new things and work in untraditional ways. If only considering a company's official org chart, they may fail. The informal organization can be more important for getting UX done.

/videos/learning-ux-doing-ux/.title: Learning UX by Doing UX
/videos/learning-ux-doing-ux/.summary: The best way to learn UX is by *doing* UX. Knowing some theory and concepts is key, but superior skills are built by reflecting upon the outcome of practicing the skill.

/videos/what-makes-a-dark-ui-pattern/.title: What Makes a Dark UI Pattern?
/videos/what-makes-a-dark-ui-pattern/.summary: Dark design patterns intentionally trick users into doing things they don't want to do. This is different than persuasive UX which nudges users without deception.

/videos/responding-to-unhelpful-design-f.title: Responding to Unhelpful Design Feedback
/videos/responding-to-unhelpful-design-f.summary: In UX design meetings, critiques are sometimes based on hypothetical scenarios and pseudoevidence: not actual user problems, but something that *might* happen.

/videos/4-factors-of-ux-maturity/.title: The 4 Factors of UX Maturity
/videos/4-factors-of-ux-maturity/.summary: 4 main factors (and 12 subfactors) should be considered to assess an organization's UX maturity: strategy, culture, process, and outcomes.

/videos/improving-decision-making-journa.title: Improving Your Decision-Making With Journaling
/videos/improving-decision-making-journa.summary: Keep a journal to document the decisions in your UX work, and once the outcome is known, return to your journal to reflect on how to improve next time.

/videos/writing-for-social-media/.title: Writing for Social Media
/videos/writing-for-social-media/.summary: Content usability applies to social media copywriting, and legibility requirements are high since users often scroll through their feeds at high speed.

/videos/observers-person-and-remote-usab.title: Handling Observers in User Research
/videos/observers-person-and-remote-usab.summary: Design team members should observe user research sessions, but this should be planned and managed to avoid having the observers distract and bias the study participants.

/videos/making-design-improvements/.title: Making Design Improvements vs. Upsetting Established Users
/videos/making-design-improvements/.summary: Even if a design change improves the overall user experience, it can frustrate existing users who are used to things working a certain way.

/videos/group-dynamics-ux-teams/.title: Group Dynamics in UX Teams
/videos/group-dynamics-ux-teams/.summary: How to move from an uncommitted group to a high-performance UX design team through the 5 phases of team development.

/videos/assessing-user-reactions-visual-.title: Assessing User Reactions to Visual Design
/videos/assessing-user-reactions-visual-.summary: 4 user research methods for assessing visual design (and when and why to use each): preference explanation, open & closed word choice, and numerical rankings for brand attributes.

/videos/confirmation-bias-ux-work/.title: Confirmation Bias in UX Work
/videos/confirmation-bias-ux-work/.summary: Confirmation bias is the tendency to preferentially seek out or believe data that confirms your expectations. For example, thinking that one part of the UI is well designed and another is bad, might you give more weight to observations of usability test participants having trouble with that second feature.

/videos/mouse-king/.title: Mouse Is King
/videos/mouse-king/.summary: The computer mouse is the most efficient pointing device for speed and accuracy. More important, it's the symbol of user empowerment and control over the user interface.

/videos/ux-maturity-model-stages/.title: UX Maturity Model Stages
/videos/ux-maturity-model-stages/.summary: Companies and organizations progress through 6 stages as user experience becomes more systematic and integrated with development and corporate goals/budgets. From stage 1 (absent) to stage 6 (user-driven), we give tips for recognizing your current stage and how to move up a level.

/videos/self-determination-theory-autono.title: Self-Determination Theory: Users Want Autonomy, Relatedness, and Competency
/videos/self-determination-theory-autono.summary: Humans have a deep need for autonomy, relatedness, and competency in their life. Catering to these needs in UX design can drastically increase user satisfaction.

/videos/ux-documentation-agile/.title: UX Documentation in Agile
/videos/ux-documentation-agile/.summary: Documenting UX processes and design decisions are organizational memory, so even Agile projects that emphasize minimal documentation benefit from two cases of lightweight UX documentation.

/videos/prioritize-ux-findings-severity/.title: Prioritize UX Findings by Severity
/videos/prioritize-ux-findings-severity/.summary: When reporting design issues after usability studies or heuristic evaluation, assign severity ratings based on a small set of criteria.

/videos/probing-user-interviews/.title: Probing in User Interviews
/videos/probing-user-interviews/.summary: Follow-up questions in user interviews gather more detailed information from participants than they provided in their initial answers to our planned questions. This video provides examples of two main forms of probing questions.

/videos/content-management-model/.title: Content Management Models
/videos/content-management-model/.summary: There are 3 ways to structure digital content production in an organization: centralized (a single team owns creation, management, and publication) or decentralized (domain experts manage their own content), as well as hybrids between these two.

/videos/design-tool-does-not-make-design.title: The Design Tool Does Not Make the Designer
/videos/design-tool-does-not-make-design.summary: There are many design tools, and new ones come out all the time. Finding a single tool to do the job is not likely, so focus instead on understanding core design principles and adapting your process to best fit a particular task.

/videos/creating-ux-research-plan/.title: Creating a UX Research Plan
/videos/creating-ux-research-plan/.summary: Before starting any user research project, write down a research plan, preferably using a template that ensures that you don't overlook something. This keeps stakeholders informed and structures your own thinking.

/videos/what-are-contextual-inquiries/.title: What Are Contextual Inquiries?
/videos/what-are-contextual-inquiries/.summary: Contextual inquiry is a user research method that is helpful to define requirements, improve processes, learn what's important to users, and spark ideas for future projects.

/videos/how-practice-empathy/.title: How to Practice Empathy
/videos/how-practice-empathy/.summary: Understanding and sharing the needs and motivations of users will lead to better design decisions. Observational research should be nonjudgmental while keeping an open mind and reducing bias.

/videos/user-research-non-existent-produ.title: User Research for Nonexistent Products
/videos/user-research-non-existent-produ.summary: If your product doesn't exist yet, and you don't even have a prototype, you can (and should) still base design decisions on user research. Observational research methods can gather information about user needs and provide input to new-product ideation.

/videos/digital-wayfinding/.title: Digital Wayfinding
/videos/digital-wayfinding/.summary: Wayfinding cues like districts and landmarks help residents and tourists find their way around cities. The same ideas can help users of digital products (e.g., websites) understand where they are and where they can go.

/videos/discovery-mapping-methods/.title: Discovery Mapping Methods
/videos/discovery-mapping-methods/.summary: Mapping can help UX practitioners synthesize insight into one place and visualize the problem space. This video covers 3 maps that are often utilized during the discovery phase of a UX design project: ecosystem maps, experience maps, and process maps.

/videos/tips-new-ux-researchers-remote-i.title: Tips for New UX Researchers Carrying Out Remote Interviews
/videos/tips-new-ux-researchers-remote-i.summary: Doing your very first remote user interview? Our UX intern has tips for conquering your nerves and getting great research results.

/videos/3-types-roadmaps/.title: 3 Types of Roadmaps
/videos/3-types-roadmaps/.summary: Roadmaps cover future work and vision, but this can be done at different scopes, from everything related to the product to only the UX activities and priorities, possibly narrowed to a sub-specialty of UX.

/videos/management-vs-craft/.title: Management vs. Craft: UX Needs to Value Both
/videos/management-vs-craft/.summary: Dual career ladders are important in user experience. Don't force talented UX professionals to become managers if their growth path would instead benefit from focusing on UX craft.

/videos/service-blueprinting-frustration.title: Overcoming Service-Blueprinting Frustrations
/videos/service-blueprinting-frustration.summary: Our research with UX practitioners found 3 main areas of frustration with service-blueprint projects. Here are recommendations for overcoming or alleviating these problems.

/videos/contextual-inquiry-pitfalls/.title: Problems with Contextual Inquiries
/videos/contextual-inquiry-pitfalls/.summary: Contextual inquiry is a UX research method where you shadow people as they do their job (or leisure tasks), allowing you to ask questions in context. This video provides advice on overcoming the main challenges with this method.

/videos/sympathy-vs-empathy-ux/.title: Sympathy vs. Empathy in UX
/videos/sympathy-vs-empathy-ux/.summary: Sympathy acknowledges that users are having difficulties, but empathy goes further by understanding the users' needs and motivations.

/videos/ux-research-made-agile/.title: UX Research Made Agile
/videos/ux-research-made-agile/.summary: Test early and often is a key recommendation for UX research. Dora Brune shares her approach, including regular Open Test Labs to engage more product teams and make user research more agile. Kinder Eggs make for a nice warmup task, even in remote tests. (Recorded at a participant panel at the UX Conference.)

/videos/ethnography-ux/.title: Ethnography in UX
/videos/ethnography-ux/.summary: Good UX design requires understanding the context and patterns of human behavior, especially in new products or features that solve real needs. The 5 steps to rapid corporate ethnography lead you to these discoveries.

/videos/reciprocation-vs-reward/.title: Reciprocation: Why Login Walls Aren’t Always “Better"
/videos/reciprocation-vs-reward/.summary: The reciprocity principle states that people, when given something upfront, tend to feel a sense of obligation to repay what has been provided. Login walls reverse this sequence and require users to disclose personal info before allowing access to content. People often resent this, and may not be as forthcoming or cooperative as a result.

/videos/using-translator-during-usabilit.title: Using a Translator During Usability Testing
/videos/using-translator-during-usabilit.summary: Usability studies with international users can be very informative, but if you don't speak the foreign language, you will need interpretation to understand the user (and for the user to understand you). These 5 guidelines will improve the value of translated research sessions.

/videos/ux-roadmaps-6-steps/.title: UX Roadmaps in 6 Steps
/videos/ux-roadmaps-6-steps/.summary: A roadmap documents upcoming and future priorities for your user experience. The process starts with gathering goals, proceeds through the creation and sharing of the UX roadmap, and never ends, since the last step is to update.

/videos/context-adds-value-ux-artifacts/.title: Context Adds Value to UX Artifacts
/videos/context-adds-value-ux-artifacts/.summary: In a museum, knowing the backstory of an artifact makes it more interesting. Similarly, in a UX project, you can make better decisions when you know the context of your UX artifacts like journey maps and wireframes.

/videos/repeated-user-actions-are-frustr.title: Repeated User Actions Are Frustrating
/videos/repeated-user-actions-are-frustr.summary: It's frustrating for users to go back-and-forth and back-and-forth to the same web page, bouncing around without getting what they need. Analytics data can help identify pages that don't help users progress.

/videos/level-up-your-visual-design-skil.title: 3 Ways to Level Up Your Visual Design Skills
/videos/level-up-your-visual-design-skil.summary: Designers, researchers, and generalists alike can improve their visual design skills through creative exercises focused on identification, replication, or exploration.

/videos/top-10-web-design-mistakes/.title: Top 10 Web-Design Mistakes
/videos/top-10-web-design-mistakes/.summary: Jakob Nielsen condemns 10 awful design flaws that plague today's websites, as voted by the audience at his Virtual UX Conference keynote.

/videos/product-ux-partnerships/.title: Product & UX Partnerships
/videos/product-ux-partnerships/.summary: Product management and user experience should partner throughout product development. But how? Here are 5 tips.

/videos/aesthetic-usability-effect/.title: The Aesthetic Usability Effect and Prioritizing Appearance vs. Functionality
/videos/aesthetic-usability-effect/.summary: Users believe that designs that look good also work well, and UX should take advantage of this. But don't make aesthetic usability lead you astray as a designer, because the UI must actually work well for long-term success.

/videos/better-ux-deliverables/.title: Better UX Deliverables
/videos/better-ux-deliverables/.summary: Communicating UX work and findings to the full team, stakeholders, and leadership requires engaging deliverables. Amanda Gulley shared her experience improving the design and usability of UX deliverables at a UX Conference participant panel.

/videos/design-thinking-learners-journey.title: Design Thinking Learner's Journey
/videos/design-thinking-learners-journey.summary: Research with people who are learning Design Thinking shows that they progress in a nonlinear manner through 4 phases of increasing competency and confidence. Understanding these phases helps both learners and educators/managers.

/videos/enterprise-user-experience/.title: Enterprise User Experience
/videos/enterprise-user-experience/.summary: Trends for improving the user experience for enterprise software and other internal design projects.

/videos/sell-ux-translating-business-val.title: How to Sell UX: Translating UX to Business Value
/videos/sell-ux-translating-business-val.summary: We speak users, whereas stakeholders speak business. We must translate: "if we do this for the user, it'll do that for the business."

/videos/short-term-memory-ui-design/.title: Short-Term Memory Limitations Impact User Interface Design
/videos/short-term-memory-ui-design/.summary: People can only hold a small amount of information in their short-term memory, which fades fast. These facts impact most aspects of screen design and dictate many usability guidelines.

/videos/advanced-user-testing-methods/.title: Advanced User Testing Methods for Accelerating Innovation
/videos/advanced-user-testing-methods/.summary: Two user research methods allow you to quickly test a large number of design alternatives, thus accelerating UX innovation. Rapid iterative design and within-subjects testing of multiple alternate designs aren't for every project but are great when they do apply.

/videos/working-memory-external-memory/.title: Working Memory and External Memory
/videos/working-memory-external-memory/.summary: People have very limited ability to keep information in their working memory while performing tasks, so user interfaces should be designed accordingly: to minimize memory load. One way of doing so is to offload items to external memory by showing them on the screen.

/videos/limited-usability-testing-busine.title: Limited Usability Testing and Business Decisions
/videos/limited-usability-testing-busine.summary: Some business stakeholders say that 5 test users can't represent all customers, and so it's too dangerous to release a new design. Better to keep existing workflows unchanged. How to respond to such claims.

/videos/recruiting-expert-users-usabilit.title: Recruiting Expert Users as Usability Study Participants
/videos/recruiting-expert-users-usabilit.summary: User research, especially for complex apps and domain-specific design, may require study participants with high expertise who can be difficult to recruit. Here are 5 tips for getting expert users.

/videos/first-online-ux-internship/.title: First Online UX Internship
/videos/first-online-ux-internship/.summary: Our UX intern, Ambika Tripathi, gives advice on how to succeed when interning in an all-remote UX team.

/videos/separate-ux-backlogs-agile/.title: Separate UX Backlogs in Agile
/videos/separate-ux-backlogs-agile/.summary: Agile development teams that struggle to keep track of UX work in the product backlog can utilize a separate backlog for UX. This method can help siloed teams where UX and development aren't in direct communication. Separate UX backlogs do have pros and cons, which are discussed here.

/videos/social-proof-ux/.title: Social Proof in UX
/videos/social-proof-ux/.summary: Users take cues from other humans: if many others like something or do something, that makes people feel that this thing must be good.

/videos/triangulation-combine-findings-m.title: Triangulation: Combine Findings from Multiple User Research Methods
/videos/triangulation-combine-findings-m.summary: Improve design decisions by looking at the problem from multiple points of view: combine multiple types of data or data from several UX research methods.

/videos/designers-identity/.title: A Designer's Identity
/videos/designers-identity/.summary: What does it mean to be a "designer?" Let's broaden the definition, based on the purpose, not the discipline. (Keynote by our Chief Designer, Sarah Gibbons)

/videos/translating-ux-concepts-design-p.title: Translating UX Concepts into Design Practice
/videos/translating-ux-concepts-design-p.summary: Edgar Anzaldua presents a 6-year case study of learning and applying ever-more subtle UX concepts and growing his influence. Always something new to learn, from junior to senior professional level.

/videos/dont-overthink-ux-roi/.title: Don't Overthink UX ROI
/videos/dont-overthink-ux-roi/.summary: It can be hard to calculate the return on investment (ROI) for user experience design improvements. But don't get bogged down in less-important details: often simple metrics can give a good-enough estimate to justify UX investments.

/videos/video-game-design-ux/.title: Video Game Design and User Experience
/videos/video-game-design-ux/.summary: Video game design is a special case of user interface design, with some differences (especially in user goals) but also many similarities with more traditional UX design problems and methods.

/videos/big-tables-small-screens/.title: How to Fit Big Tables on Small Screens
/videos/big-tables-small-screens/.summary: No matter your screen size, some data tables will be too big for the screen. This problem is particularly common on mobile devices. Simple interaction techniques can help, but you may need to offer users more advanced features for information hiding and column reordering.

/videos/document-ux-methods/.title: Identify and Document Your UX Methods
/videos/document-ux-methods/.summary: For each research or design method you employ, create a document that defines this method and can be used to educate other team members on UX activities.

/videos/breaking-out-content-silo/.title: Breaking out of the Content Silo
/videos/breaking-out-content-silo/.summary: Coming from a traditional content/writing background, Michelle Blake presents her case study of broadening her remit to a fuller range of user-experience issues and improving the design of her organization's website.

/videos/fittss-law-links-buttons/.title: Using Fitts's Law to Make Links and Buttons Easier to Click
/videos/fittss-law-links-buttons/.summary: Fitts's Law describes how long time it takes to click a target, based on the distance to the target and its size. Use this information to make buttons and links faster to click.
